The ATC building would absolutely be a positive impact for the neighborhood, but it MUST be done well or I will push back heavily. This is a risky development I am nervous about that could be very bad for the neighborhood for decades IF executed poorly. 

1. The building must compliment the character of the neighborhood. It must be aesthetically pleasing. the design must be timeless. There are too many examples of community centers in the area that quickly become old/outdated in design and materials. The Georgia Hill Center right up the street is an example of this. It is largely not a good design that adds to the character of the neighborhood, or a great use of land. 

2. It must not interfere with parking spots on Connally or adjacent streets. Putting an industrial-sized building right next to residential properties risks creating a dead-zone surrounding it. No one wants to live in the shadow of a stadium, highway, factory, etc. This could have a similar impact for the surrounding streets and push down property value IF done incorrectly. STREET LEVEL ACTIVATION is a need-to-have here. 

3. If additional parking is created, it should be minimized in scope and be done with high-quality, natural material in order to reduce flooding risk. Eco-parking lots prioritize gravel, native plantings, and appropriate lighting. I will push back heavily if a plain old black-tarmac design is proposed. 

Ultimately, I do see the value in gaining more neighborhood stewardship of the land similar to the Grant Park Conservancy. There may have been a precedent for APS ownership in the past given the struggling nature of the neighborhood, but we are now a thriving neighborhood capable of community involvement and stewardship.
